_comment: Scenarios of the synthetic behavioral suite. 'expect' is what the pipeline must do with the scenario's tagged segment(s): skip = a skip covering it; keep = an integration marker, no skip; label = a label-only marker (show), no skip; none = no segment of any kind on it; noskip = a label or nothing, never a skip. Scenarios 1-18 come from Atishay's starting list, 19-20 from his follow-up, 21-25 were added (see 'origin').

scenarios.name: Classic mid-roll
scenarios.brief: A mid-video read that opens with explicit disclosure ('this video is sponsored by X', 'today's sponsor is X') and ends with a code or link. Tag the read from the disclosure sentence to the last pitch sentence.

scenarios.name: Soft segue
scenarios.brief: The read is entered through a topical bridge ('speaking of staying safe online...', 'and that is exactly why I...'). The bridge sentence(s) belong to the ad and are tagged; the content sentence before the bridge is not.

scenarios.name: Question segue
scenarios.brief: The read starts with a question to the audience or a co-host ('do you know who today's sponsor is?', 'ever wondered how much of your data is out there?'). Tag from the question.

scenarios.name: Cold-open ad
scenarios.brief: The read starts within the first 30 seconds (a hook sentence or two, then the ad, or the ad first), then the video proper begins.

scenarios.name: Two sponsors back to back
scenarios.brief: Two different brands read one right after the other with no content between. Two tagged segments (one per brand), each 'skip'.

scenarios.name: Ad after the outro
scenarios.brief: The creator wraps up ('thanks for watching, see you next week') and THEN does a sponsor read as the very last thing.

scenarios.name: No disclosure words
scenarios.brief: A plain pitch with no 'sponsor', 'partner', 'brought to you' or 'ad': the product, its benefits, and a code or link ('use code MAYA for 20% off at brand.com/maya'). Description may or may not have a sponsor line.

scenarios.name: Misheard brand
scenarios.brief: A normal read whose brand is spelled the way auto-captions mishear it, in BOTH variants (e.g. 'Odoo' -> 'Udo', 'Squarespace' -> 'square space', 'Raycon' -> 'ray con'). The description spells it right on a sponsor line.

scenarios.name: Long read across a window edge
scenarios.brief: A read longer than 3 minutes (about 550+ words of pitch) that starts around 2:30-3:30 into the video, so it crosses the 4:00 analysis-window edge. One tagged segment. Total transcript ~8 minutes.

scenarios.name: Integration
scenarios.brief: The creator uses the product to do the video's actual task (edits the video in the editor, builds the website on the builder, navigates with the app), with a light disclosure ('thanks to X for sponsoring this part'). No hard topic break, no promo-code pitch. Tag the usage span as 'keep'.

scenarios.name: Creator's own brand work
scenarios.brief: The creator tells, as part of the story, about a paid shoot or campaign they did for a brand ('today we're shooting for Fossil's new watch campaign'), without pitching it to the audience. No code, link or call to action. Tag the mention as 'none'.

scenarios.name: Brand is the subject
scenarios.brief: The whole video reviews or investigates a product or company (a VPN review, the history of a startup). The brand is named many times and appears in the title. Tag one dense mention passage as 'none'.

scenarios.name: Sponsor disclaimer
scenarios.brief: A spoken disclaimer: 'VPN companies sometimes sponsor this channel, but this video isn't sponsored and nobody saw it before you.' Tag the disclaimer as 'none'.

scenarios.name: Ad-like content
scenarios.brief: Content that sounds like an ad but is the topic: a coding tutorial where 'use code' means program code, a deals-explainer that reads out what a store's discount codes do, a scam-awareness video quoting a fake pitch. Tag the ad-like passage as 'none'.

scenarios.name: Self-promo
scenarios.brief: The creator promotes their own merch, Patreon, course or membership. Tag it 'label' with category selfpromo (or membership).

scenarios.name: Affiliate link
scenarios.brief: The creator mentions the gear they use with 'links in the description are affiliate links, I get a small commission'. Not a paid read. Tag it 'label' with category affiliate.

scenarios.name: Paid charity spot
scenarios.brief: A charity or NGO paid for the spot: 'This episode is brought to you by <charity>', its mission, how to donate or visit. Tag 'skip', category sponsor.

scenarios.name: Non-English read (Hindi)
scenarios.brief: A Hindi video (Devanagari, the way Hindi auto-captions write English loanwords: 'वीडियो', 'स्पॉन्सर', 'डिस्काउंट') with a sponsor read. Every sentence also carries 'en', an English translation like YouTube's auto-translation. lang 'hi'.

scenarios.name: Description disclaimer, no ad
scenarios.brief: The description carries a standing disclaimer about sponsors ('Viewer discretion is advised regarding the products of sponsors advertised on our platforms; we take no responsibility...'), but the video has no ad at all. Tag one ordinary passage that mentions a product in passing as 'none'. Must give no description hint and no skip.

scenarios.name: 'Sponsors' in conversation
scenarios.brief: The word 'sponsor(s)' comes up in the story itself (a race team's sponsors, a sponsored athlete, 'our school fair got local sponsors'). No ad. Tag that passage as 'none'.

scenarios.name: Podcast with sponsors spread out
scenarios.brief: A podcast episode (two hosts or host + guest, conversational) with a pre-roll read near the start and two mid-roll reads for different brands later, each separated by conversation. Three tagged 'skip' segments. Total ~6 minutes.

scenarios.name: Podcast ad break, reads back to back
scenarios.brief: A podcast where the host announces a break ('let's take a quick break to thank our sponsors') and reads three different sponsors in a row, then returns to the conversation. Tag each read as its own 'skip' segment (the announcement belongs to the first).

scenarios.name: Integration ending in a pitch
scenarios.brief: The creator uses the product inside the content (tag 'keep'), then turns to camera and pitches it with a code and link (tag 'skip', a second segment). Only the pitch may skip.

scenarios.name: Read plus a reminder
scenarios.brief: A full read mid-video and a short reminder at the end ('thanks again to X for supporting this video, 20% off at x.com/code'). Two tagged 'skip' segments; the reminder is at least ~8 seconds.

scenarios.name: Disclosure line, no read
scenarios.brief: A single sentence 'Part of this video is sponsored by X.' and nothing else about X anywhere. Tag that sentence 'noskip' (category sponsor): it may be labeled or left alone, but never skipped.
